messages.subject: normal() + comma = normal_log()
parts:
Another stupid error of mine:

model {
  z_log_earn ~ normal(z_beta[1] + z_beta[2] * z_height, + z_beta[3] * z_male, z_sigma);
}

I left a comma after z_height, when I added the last predictor.
The model did non compile, of course, but I got this message:

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="normal_log"

It looks a bit strange, doesn't it?

Thanks

Sergio

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] normal() + comma = normal_log()
parts:
On 7/27/13 11:45 AM, sp_r...@yahoo.it wrote:
> Another stupid error of mine:
>
> model {
> z_log_earn ~ normal(z_beta[1] + z_beta[2] * z_height, + z_beta[3] * z_male, z_sigma);
> }
>
> I left a comma after z_height, when I added the last predictor.
> The model did non compile, of course, but I got this message:
>
> DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
> no matches for function name="normal_log"
>
> It looks a bit strange, doesn't it?

The problem is that (+ a * b) is a well-formed
expression, so the parser took you to be specifying
three arguments to normal().

In general,

y ~ foo(theta1,...,thetaN);

compiles as:

lp__ <- lp__ + foo_log(y,theta1,...,thetaN)

So the function getting called is the _log version.
We should try to make that message clearer. Someone else
already filed an issue about changing our manual to make this
relationship clearer in the doc of every distribution.

- Bob
